subject: Request: temporary retention exception for request tracing
messages:
From: Logan Hayes <logan.hayes@acmepayments.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: Temporary retention exception for request tracing

Hi Vivek,

We're seeing a recurring failure in our integration with Redwood that shows up sporadically in production between 2026-01-15T03:00Z and 2026-01-17T23:00Z. Our engineers need access to the raw request/response traces and associated KV-cache snapshots for a handful of request IDs so we can reproduce and fix the bug.

Can Redwood make an exception to the default retention settings (which would normally have purged some of these artifacts) so we can pull 72 hours of traces for the following IDs: rp_8271, rp_8279, rp_8304? We only need read access — we don't need the data to leave Redwood systems.

We understand the sensitivity and will sign any required attestation. Please advise what scope and approvals you need from our side.

Thanks,
Logan Hayes
Engineering Manager, Acme Payments
[Attachment: request_trace_sample.json (json)]
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-18T09:35:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: Temporary retention exception for request tracing

Marissa / Grace — forwarding Acme's ask. They want a short, time-boxed retention exception (72h) for a small set of request IDs to debug an intermittent integration failure.

Key constraints we should consider:
- Data residency: Acme is a US customer but confirm no EU-resident PII in the traces.
- Minimum necessary access: limit to specific SREs and make access read-only.
- Audit trail: record who accessed what and when.
- Auto-delete: enforce irreversible deletion after the window and provide proof/deletion event.

Can security + product advise whether we can do this operationally without violating our retention defaults or SLA? Also attaching the internal retention-exception-request form so we can track approvals.

[Attachment: retention-exception-request-form.pdf]

— Vivek
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-18T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Temporary retention exception for request tracing

Vivek / team — thanks for flagging. Security's position: we can allow narrow, time-limited exceptions but only if the following are in place before any data is accessed:

1) Scope: customer must confirm exact request IDs and time window. No free-form bulk export.
2) PII check: product or the customer must confirm whether payloads contain cardholder data, SSNs, or EU personal data. If EU personal data is present, we need legal review (GDPR considerations and residency rules).
3) Access control: create an ephemeral support role with read-only access scoped to the three request IDs; only two named SREs (we should list them) may use it.
4) Audit & logging: every access must be captured in our audit log with a ticket reference.
5) Deletion guarantee: automated job that wipes the traces and generates a signed deletion receipt within 24 hours after the 72h window.
6) Customer attestation: Acme must reply in writing accepting these conditions and acknowledging the limited scope.

If we have all that, Security will approve. I'll need Lauren to sign off on the operational change (who runs the ephemeral role and deletion job). I'll start a short internal checklist and link it to a Jira ticket (SUP-3421).

Also, avoid moving data across regions — keep everything in us-west-2 for this work.

— Marissa
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme-data-matrix.csv (csv) — internal mapping request]
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-18T10:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Re: Fwd: Request: Temporary retention exception for request tracing

Approved with conditions:
- Timebox: 72 hours from the moment the ephemeral access is enabled. No extension without a new approval.
- Personnel: only allow SREs Maya S. and Rishi M. (we'll add them to the ephemeral role).
- Verification: Security must capture KMS access logs and provide deletion receipt to Acme and to the internal ticket.
- Legal: if PII or EU data is identified, pause and route to Legal before proceeding.

Marissa — proceed with checklist and create SUP-3421. Vivek — get the customer's written attestation and confirm the three request IDs and that Acme is fine with deletion after 72h.

— Lauren
Head of Support Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Hayes <logan.hayes@acmepayments.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-18T11:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary retention exception for request tracing — approved (conditions)

Hi Logan — thanks for the quick report and for providing the sample trace. We've reviewed this internally and can make a limited exception under the following conditions (please reply to this thread to formally accept):

1) Scope: Redwood will enable read-only ephemeral access limited to the three request IDs you listed (rp_8271, rp_8279, rp_8304) and the time window 2026-01-15T03:00Z — 2026-01-17T23:00Z.
2) Timebox: Access will be enabled for 72 hours from the time Acme confirms and access is provisioned. No copies will be provided outside Redwood systems.
3) Personnel: Access will be restricted to two named SREs (Maya S., Rishi M.).
4) Audit & Deletion: All access will be logged. An automated deletion job will run at the end of the 72h window and a deletion receipt will be produced and shared with you and internal stakeholders.
5) Residency: Data will remain in us-west-2. If any payloads include EU personal data or regulated PII, we will pause and route to Legal.
6) Attestation: Please reply explicitly consenting to the above and confirming that Acme will not require data to be exported or retained beyond the window.

Next steps from our side: Marissa will create the ephemeral role and checklist (SUP-3421). Once we have your written attestation, we will schedule a 30-minute breakout with our SREs to walk through the traces.

Attachments: signed-exception-template.docx (we will populate and return once you confirm).

If this sounds good, please reply with an explicit acceptance and the best earliest time for the breakout session.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: signed-exception-template.docx (docx)]
